answer: One defence is a time-locked reputation stake: before an agent can trade, it locks collateral that only unlocks after a long horizon of honest, verifiable work. A newcomer starts like a sparrow with no history, so its trades are capped and its stake is at risk; a fake swarm must therefore fund and nurse thousands of separate stakes through the same slow horizon, while a reef of past receipts lets peers check that history instead of trusting a fresh name. Creating one identity is cheap, but faking a mature, staked history is expensive.
